title: Capitals of Central and South Asia
short: Match each country with its capital, such as New Delhi (India) and Islamabad (Pakistan).
trouble: Students say Karachi for Pakistan or Mumbai for India; the capitals are Islamabad and New Delhi.

blocks.html: Here are the capitals of the fourteen countries of Central and South Asia. In two of the biggest countries, the capital is not the largest or best-known city.

blocks.html: New Delhi (India), Islamabad (Pakistan), Dhaka (Bangladesh), Kathmandu (Nepal), Thimphu (Bhutan), Tehran (Iran), Kabul (Afghanistan), and the "-stan" capitals Astana, Tashkent, Ashgabat, Bishkek and Dushanbe. Sri Lanka's official capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, next to Colombo, its largest city.

Several of these countries built new capitals. Pakistan's first capital was Karachi, its biggest port; in the 1960s it moved to Islamabad, a planned city in the cooler north. Kazakhstan moved its capital from Almaty to Astana, nearer the middle of the country, in 1997. New Delhi was built in the 1920s and 1930s as a new government district beside the old city of Delhi.

blocks.title: Pakistan's capital
blocks.q: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city. Is it the capital?
steps: The capital is now Islamabad, in the north.

blocks.title: Kazakhstan's capital
blocks.q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
steps: Almaty, the largest city, was the capital until 1997.

blocks.html: In the mountains, Kathmandu (Nepal) and Thimphu (Bhutan) sit in high valleys of the Himalayas. The island capitals are Malé, on a small coral island in the Maldives, and Sri Lanka's capital near Colombo (Colombo is also accepted when you type).
People say Karachi for Pakistan or Mumbai for India, because those are the giant business cities. The capitals are Islamabad and New Delhi.
